literal: Those who are destitute (acc.) trusting let one avoid; for they, attachment they are without, they will not be ashamed of blame.
translation: Avoid trusting those who are destitute and without ties. Since they have no attachments, they will not be ashamed of incurring blame.
modern: எந்தப் பற்றுக்கோடும் இல்லாதவர்களை நம்பி ஒரு பொறுப்பை ஒப்படைப்பதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும். ஏனென்றால், அவர்கள் சமூகத்தின் மீதோ நற்பெயரின் மீதோ பற்று இல்லாதவர்கள் என்பதால், பழிச்சொல்லுக்கு வெட்கப்பட மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet advises against placing trust in people who have nothing to lose. The word 'aṟṟār' can mean those who are financially destitute or those who lack social and moral ties; in the context of choosing whom to trust, it refers to those without roots or standing. Because such people have no meaningful attachments ('paṟṟu') to society, family, or reputation, they do not fear the consequences of their actions. Consequently, they will not feel ashamed of committing faults or facing public blame ('paḻi').
